title.justification: The paper's focus is on the effect of technologically-assisted communication on inter-brain synchrony, as highlighted by the title. This is the main topic explored throughout the study.

extractions.description: The paper investigates the impact of technologically-assisted communication on brain-to-brain synchrony using hyperscanning EEG in mother-child interactions, comparing live face-to-face interaction and remote communication. The study examines inter-brain connectivity, social behavior associations, and discusses the implications of reduced inter-brain synchrony during technological communication, especially concerning 'Zoom fatigue' and potential impacts on social cognition development.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily explores the neuroscientific aspects of inter-brain connectivity in technologically-assisted communications without focusing on broad climate or ecological sustainable development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: The transition to technologically-assisted communication has permeated all facets of human social life; yet, its impact on the social brain is still unknown and the effects may be particularly intense during periods of developmental transitions.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not address any categories directly related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, instead focusing on neuroscience and communication.
primary_category.quote: Technologically-assisted communication has its drawbacks, among which is the reported 'Zoom fatigue', the manifestation of tiredness associated with virtual communication.

secondary_categories.justification: As the paper does not link to any auxiliary or indirect Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development categories, no secondary category is applicable here.
secondary_categories.quote: Support perspectives suggest that daily face-focused interactions tune humans’ social brain through bottom-up bio-behavioral processes and add the dimension of inter-brain connectedness.

primary_sub_category.justification: The study does not fit into any specific sub-categories related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_sub_category.quote: Our findings clearly demonstrate the price we pay for technology.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No secondary sub-categories are relevant to this paper as it does not touch on any facets of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: The gains to social development, empathic abilities, and brain maturation afforded by face-to-face interactions may not translate to technological encounters.

applications.justification: There are no specific applications related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development elaborated in the paper.
applications.quote: Our findings suggest that the gains to social development, empathic abilities, and brain maturation afforded by face-to-face interactions may not translate to technological encounters.

new_primary_category.justification: The topic does not warrant a new category within the realm of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
new_primary_category.quote: We are only beginning to understand how social technology impacts the human social brain and this topic is in urgent need of further research.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: Similarly, no new sub-category is necessary as the content is unrelated to Climate or Ecological Sustainability topics.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We need to understand the cross-brain consequences of technological communication at different stages of child development and with different familiar and unfamiliar partners.
